text: What are the main sections of a basic C# console application structure?
options: Importing section, Namespace Declaration, Class Declaration, Main() method
Package Declaration, Interface Implementation, Main() method
Module Import, Function Definition, Execution Block
facts: A basic C# console application typically includes an importing section, namespace declaration, class declaration, and a Main() method.
The importing section uses `using` directives to include necessary namespaces.
The `namespace` keyword declares a scope that contains a set of related objects.
The `class` contains methods and data members; the `Main()` method is the entry point of a C# console application.

text: What is the entry point of a C# console application?
facts: Every C# console application starts execution from the Main() method.
The Main() method can optionally accept an array of strings as arguments.
It is defined as static, meaning it can be called without instantiating the class.
examples: static void Main(string[] args) { Console.WriteLine("Hello World"); }

text: Which keyword is used to include namespaces in a C# program?
facts: The 'using' directive allows the use of types in a namespace without specifying the full path.
It is commonly used at the top of C# files.
It helps improve code readability and reduces verbosity.

text: In a C# console application, what is the purpose of the 'namespace' keyword?
facts: Namespaces group logically related classes and types.
They help avoid name conflicts and organize code.
The keyword 'namespace' is used to declare a namespace.

text: Which method signature correctly represents the Main() method in a C# console app?
facts: The correct and most common signature is static void Main(string[] args).
It is static so the runtime can call it without creating an object.
It returns void and can optionally take command-line arguments.

text: What will the output of Console.WriteLine("Hello World"); be?
options: Print Hello World to the output window
It will throw a runtime error
facts: Console.WriteLine prints text to the standard output (typically the console window).
It automatically adds a newline at the end of the output.
It is part of the System namespace.

text: Which method is used to read a single character from the console in C#?
facts: Console.ReadKey() reads the next character or function key pressed by the user.
It returns a ConsoleKeyInfo object, which includes information about the pressed key.

text: Which method is used to read the next line of characters from the standard input stream?
facts: Console.ReadLine() reads the next line of characters from the standard input stream.
It returns the input as a string.

text: Which method is used to write a line terminator to the standard output stream?
facts: Console.WriteLine() writes the specified data, followed by the current line terminator, to the standard output stream.
It is commonly used to display output with a newline at the end.

text: Which property is used to get or set the background color of the console?
facts: Console.BackgroundColor gets or sets the background color of the console.
It uses the ConsoleColor enumeration.
examples: Console.Clear(); // Applies the background color to the entire console

text: Which property is used to get or set the foreground color of the console?
facts: Console.ForegroundColor gets or sets the foreground color of the console.
It uses the ConsoleColor enumeration.

text: Which method is used to clear the console buffer and corresponding console window of display information?
facts: Console.Clear() clears the console buffer and the corresponding console window of display information.
It resets the cursor position to the top-left corner of the console.

text: Which method is used to reset the console colors to their defaults?
facts: Console.ResetColor() resets the console's foreground and background colors to their defaults.
It is useful after changing colors to revert to the original settings.

text: Which property is used to get or set the cursor's row position within the console buffer area?
facts: Console.CursorTop gets or sets the row position of the cursor within the console buffer area.
The topmost row is 0.

text: Which property is used to get or set the cursor's column position within the console buffer area?
facts: Console.CursorLeft gets or sets the column position of the cursor within the console buffer area.
The leftmost column is 0.

text: Which method is used to move the cursor to the specified position?
facts: Console.SetCursorPosition(int left, int top) sets the position of the cursor.
The parameters specify the column (left) and row (top) positions.
